title: Fail-closed is the shipped default and the Weather Safety page never tells a sensorless rig what that means
what_happened: safety_fail_mode defaults to failClosed (verified in the fresh DB and at app_settings.dart:82). 'Enable weather safety' correctly defaults OFF -- but the moment a user turns it on, which reads like the responsible thing to do, a rig with no weather device and no safety monitor is treated as unsafe: the app raises a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig', and per the codebase's own WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts'. The Weather Safety page itself contains NO fail-mode control, NO row showing which weather sources are connected or what they currently read, and NO hint that zero sources are attached. The fail-mode dropdown lives on a different page (Sequencer). The rule's resolution hint literally says 'switch the safety fail mode to fail open in Settings > Automation & Safety' -- a string the user only meets at run-start, not on the page where they made the choice.
expected: The page that owns the master switch should show live source state and the fail-mode consequence. Concretely: a status row at the top ('Weather sources: none connected -- with Fail Closed, runs will park and abort'), the fail-mode selector moved next to the master switch, and turning the master switch on with zero sources should either default that rig to Warn Only or ask.
repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety. Read the whole page (3 toggles, 3 thresholds, 2 alert-timing numbers) -- nothing mentions sources or fail mode. Toggle 'Enable weather safety' on. Then go to Sequencer to find 'Safety fail mode: Fail Closed (Park)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-06-weather-safety.png and settings-obs-09-ws-scrolled.png (full page, no source/fail-mode info), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-11-sequencer.png (fail mode lives here), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png; DB safety_fail_mode|failClosed

title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
what_happened: The entire PHD2 Guiding page is Host, Port, 'PHD2 executable path (Auto-detect, optional)' and a paragraph of prose. There is no Connect/Test button, no live PHD2 connection state, no PHD2 version readout, no PHD2 profile selector, no 'launch PHD2 if not running', and no 'connect equipment in PHD2 on start'. Every other integration in this app can be verified from its settings page -- SMTP/Discord/Pushover/Telegram/generic-webhook all have 'Send test', cloud sync has 'Test Connection', both plate solvers have 'Verify', and the plate solving page even shows 'Auto-detect -- not found' inline. PHD2 is the most failure-prone dependency in the whole stack and is the only one with no verification affordance.
expected: A 'Test connection' button that opens the PHD2 event socket and reports version + current profile + connected state, and an inline auto-detect status for the executable path matching the Plate Solving page's 'Auto-detect -- not found' pattern. NINA shows PHD2's state and version inline on its guider page.
repro: Settings > search 'PHD2' > PHD2 Guiding. Read the whole page.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-73-phd2.png (whole page fits on one screen with room to spare); contrast /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-66-ps-1.png (Plate Solving's Verify + auto-detect status) and settings-obs-79-sync-1.png (cloud sync's Test Connection)
